Security policy

Source: SECURITY.md

Reporting a vulnerability

Please report security issues privately to muswaseja@gmail.com rather than in a public issue. Include the affected version, what an attacker could do, and a reproducible example if you have one. You can expect an acknowledgement within seven days.

What counts as a security issue here

knbsdata is a data-access client, so the sensitive surfaces are files, URLs and credentials rather than a running service:

  • Path traversal when extracting archives (ZIP entries escaping the destination directory).
  • Writing downloaded files outside the requested destination.
  • Credentials, tokens or cookies appearing in logs, error messages, cache metadata, download manifests or test fixtures.
  • Following a redirect to an unexpected host and treating the result as official.
  • Code execution triggered by parsing a downloaded file.
  • Silently bypassing an access control, licence acceptance or authentication step.

The last item matters as much as the others: the package must never obtain data a user is not authorised to obtain.

Handling secrets in this repository

  • Never commit credentials, tokens, cookies or .Renviron files.
  • Never store secrets in the source registry, package options persisted to disk, error logs, download manifests or test fixtures.
  • Redact personal and authentication information from any stored response fixture before committing it.
  • If a secret is committed, treat it as compromised: rotate it first, then remove it from history.
